headline: 15 mainnet contracts catalogued on Arbitrum One from official docs; all use EIP-1967 transparent proxy pattern; ProxyAdmin owner actor class not yet determined.

findings.text: D1: Arbiscan name-tag search via web search surfaced 'Ostium: Trading' at 0x6D0bA1f9996DBD8885827e1b2e8f6593e7702411 and 'Ostium: Trading Storage' at 0xcCd5891083A8acD2074690F65d3024E7D13d66E7 with EIP-1967 transparent proxy labels confirmed. Direct arbiscan.io fetch failed; evidence obtained via search snippets citing arbiscan.io pages.

D2: Official deployed contracts page at https://docs.ostium.com/protocol/security/audits lists 15 mainnet Arbitrum One contracts and 18 testnet Arbitrum Sepolia contracts. set protocol_metadata.deployed_contracts_doc to this URL.

D3: Audit page at docs.ostium.com lists 6 audit engagements: Zellic (Feb 2024, Nov 2025), ThreeSigma (Feb-Mar 2024), Pashov (Jan 2025, Apr 2025, Jan 2026). Pashov Jan 2026 review covered 13 core contracts including OstiumVault, OstiumOpenPnl, OstiumTradingCallbacks, OstiumTrading, OstiumTradingStorage, OstiumPriceRouter, OstiumPairInfos. No additional addresses beyond docs table surfaced from audit page (PDF download links not fetched due to tool-call budget).

D4: GitHub repo https://github.com/0xOstium/smart-contracts-public fetched. No hardhat-deploy deployments/ folder or broadcast/ artifacts visible at repo root. README references Hardhat but no deployment JSON artifacts found at the top-level directory listing. Pinned commit SHA not available from branch-level fetch (branch: main, no pinned SHA returned).
D5: Single chain (Arbitrum One) per protocol.chains. No multi-chain enumeration required. Arbitrum Sepolia testnet addresses also documented but excluded from admin_addresses as testnet.

D6: No factory contracts identified in the address book. Registry at 0x799a139aE56e11F0476aCE2f6118CfcAed9608d2 may enumerate child contracts; factory enumeration view call not performed due to tool-call budget exhaustion. Recorded in unknowns.

D7: Role taxonomy applied to all 15 contracts. ProxyAdmin actor_class unknown — could not determine if the ProxyAdmin's owner() is an EOA, multisig, or timelock from available evidence. Deepwiki architecture notes identify Governance Address and Manager Address as distinct roles with different privilege levels.

D8: All 15 addresses in admin_addresses trace to docs.ostium.com/protocol/security/audits (fetched this run). EIP-1967 proxy pattern for Trading and TradingStorage additionally confirmed via arbiscan.io search snippets. Implementation addresses (0xde48b32e... for Trading, 0x60c188ac... for TradingStorage) surfaced from arbiscan search snippets but not fetched as standalone URLs — recorded in unknowns per D8 rule.

rationale.verdict: Discovery run walked official docs (docs.ostium.com), deprecated GitBook docs, GitHub repo landing page, and Arbiscan search snippets. 15 mainnet Arbitrum One contracts catalogued with roles. Proxy architecture (EIP-1967 transparent) confirmed for at least Trading and TradingStorage. ProxyAdmin owner actor class, Registry child enumeration, and implementation contract addresses require follow-up on-chain reads in subsequent slices.

protocol_metadata.about: Ostium is a decentralized perpetual futures exchange deployed on Arbitrum One that enables leveraged trading of real-world assets — including equities, commodities, forex, and indices — directly from a crypto wallet using USDC as collateral. Users trade synthetic price exposure (no asset tokenization) against a single shared USDC liquidity vault (OLP vault) that acts as the counterparty when positions are imbalanced. The protocol uses a modular, upgradeable smart contract architecture (EIP-1967 transparent proxies) with oracle pricing sourced from Chainlink and Stork, and trade automation via Gelato Functions and Chainlink Automations. Ostium V2 is adapted from the Gains Network v5 codebase with significant modifications for RWA perpetuals.
